source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect and analyze emission data from Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) or Portable Emission Monitoring Systems (PEMS). Ensure that this data is recorded at regular intervals to capture the variability in emissions over time.

3. Verify the accuracy of the monitoring equipment.
Perform regular calibration and maintenance of the monitoring equipment to ensure the recorded data is accurate and reliable. Keep records of calibration, maintenance, and any equipment faults or adjustments.

4. Verify against regulatory thresholds.
Compare the monitored emission levels against the permitted thresholds set by local, regional, and national environmental regulations for each specific pollutant (e.g., particulate matter, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, etc.).

5. Document exceedances.
Record any instances where emissions levels exceed the regulatory limits. Include the date, time, duration, pollutants involved, and the recorded emission level. Also, note any potential contributing factors such as changes in production levels, equipment failures, or other unusual
